title: Unit Event — Backlight, Lens Flare — Episode4 A Step Ahead

meta.Event Outline: Wonderlands×Showtime's next step is to appear as extras in a film! Each of them is enthusiastic about this opportunity to work their magic on camera, and Rui is particularly eager to learn about a different type of directing. However, not everything goes smoothly...

rows.Line: Rental Room in Tokyo

rows.Speaker: Crew Member
rows.Line: Alright, let's take a break here!

rows.Speaker: Crew Member
rows.Line: We'll resume with Scene 32 at five sharp, so please be sure to return by them!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(Finally, a break.
That took about two hours longer than expected, but the fact we get to take one at all is a good sign.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The scene we just shot involved simply shopping for a few things, but it the choice of effects changed the impression it gave dramatically.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The supermarket was dim and gloomy in early scenes, but they turned on every light for this scene to illuminate the entire set.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Doing so, shows how Katsuyuki has changed since meeting Hajime. He's filled with much more optimism now.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(I have to credit Mr. Ohara...
It's a marvelous way to present changes in a character's emotional state.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I want to keep learning these sorts of techniques while I can, but...)
se_walk_men_002_1

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line:
Ah, Kamishiro, it's you.
Do you have a minute?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Oh, Mr. Ohara... How can I help you?

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: You said you wanted to learn more about being a director, right?

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: If that's the case, why don't you take a look at what we just shot?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: What...?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, I'd be honored.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: ...and that's the footage we just got.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I see...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: This may not sound all that profound, but seeing a set through the camera is very different from what you see with the naked eye.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: The changing camera angles between different shots must have something to do with that.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: Ah, your intuition is spot on.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: There are a myriad of differences between film and theatre, but I believe the way we make use of perspective sticks out.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Perspective...?

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: With theatre, the audience can only view the stage from a single direction. You essentially only have one camera.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line:
However, that's not the case with film.
You can use as many cameras as you like to present a space from multiple angles.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: What do you think are the benefits of that?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: It gives you the ability to control the viewer's perspective...?

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line:
Exactly.
You're limited to one camera for theatre, but film makes it easy to change how the viewer perceives what's happening.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: The scenes we shot today are a good example of that. Depending on how bright the screen is or how many shots we use, you can get the characters in the same scene to give off very different impressions.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, I see...

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: To be fair, it's difficult to produce the sort of power you get with a live performance as you do with theater...

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: But film is interesting because you can move your audience by controlling their perspective.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: Unfortunately, since most of your work involves the stage, it might be hard to put any of what I'm saying into practice.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: No.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: If anything, I'd like to learn more of these sorts of techniques.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: What?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: My dream is to put on a show that transcends borders. One that everyone can enjoy.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: And in order to make that dream come true, I need to learn as much as can about directing, no matter the medium.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: Interesting...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Which is why I want to learn about as many different ideas, techniques and thought processes as possible.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Please teach me everything you know.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line:
Hah!
Everything, huh?

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: Well, that's the energy you'll need if you're serious about this.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: I'd begun to doubt the resolve of kids like you since so many I've come across end up being spineless. But you're not like them.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: So, I'll take your word and teach you everything I can. Out of respect for that ambition.

rows.Speaker: Ohara
rows.Line: Starting tomorrow, you'll be working as my assistant. Just be warned that I'm going to be even harder on you compared to before.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Thank you very much.
I promise to do my absolute best.

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line: (I just came to take a quick peek...)

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line: (But it looks like Rui and the director are getting along really well now!)

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line:
(Things seem to be going so great!
I've gotta come back again tomorrow to give everyone whatever support I can♪)
